Subject: Actionable exceptions and QBR asks — exec clarifications needed

Team,

Thanks again for the sync this morning with Acme. They provided a short list of exec-level asks and a CSV of roadmap exceptions (attached). Before we bake anything into the QBR or our roadmap, I want to capture clear owners, drop-dead decisions, and any hard constraints from Product/Engineering. High-level asks from Acme:

- Guaranteed p95 latency target for inference pipelines under dedicated capacity (they want <120ms).
- A formal SLA addendum for data retention + audit logs (they need 7 years of retention and periodic exports).
- A path for deterministic fallback when their provisioned capacity is exhausted.

Action items I need us to clarify within 24 hours so I can respond to procurement and legal:

1) Technical feasibility: can the serving runtime deliver the p95 latency at their requested model sizes? If not, what are the tradeoffs (quantization, model variant, or batching limits)? (owner: Dev)
2) Roadmap exceptions: which of the CSV lines are blockers vs nice-to-have for Q4? Can we surface the earliest possible ETA for each? (owner: Marcus)
3) SLA language: what we can commit to for retention and export frequency without adding a heavy compliance package cost. Also note any dependencies on Dedicated vs Private deployments. (owner: Lauren)

Attachments: roadmap-exceptions.csv (from Acme), qbr-exec-asks.xlsx (compiled list), capacity-model.pdf (initial capacity estimate).

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference

On Mon, Oct 18, 2026 at 09:03 AM Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team,
> 
> Thanks again for the sync this morning with Acme. ...

Quick update from infra/runtime perspective:

- Short answer on p95: likely achievable for their medium model (7B FP16) on Dedicated with current kernels if we enforce a 1-2 request batching cap and enable KV-prefix caching. For larger models (30B+), p95 will exceed 120ms unless we accept increased cost (more GPUs or narrower quantization).
- Workarounds: serve a trimmed/quantized 13B variant or enable an optimistic routing policy to heavier nodes in our fleet (adds cost).
- Fallback behavior: we can implement deterministic fallback to a smaller model family in ~2 weeks as a runtime change, but full testing + canary rollout will be ~4-5 weeks.

Questions for Acme (cc Nora):
- Which model families / token lengths are they planning to use in production? Short prompts (<128 tokens) or long-context bursts?
- Do they require exact same semantic output when falling back, or is a best-effort acceptable?

I'll start a quick perf run with their sample payloads (if they can provide a few representative requests) and attach preliminary numbers by EOD tomorrow.

Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Evelyn / Dev —

Thanks for pulling this together. I parsed Acme's roadmap-exceptions.csv and prioritized their rows into three buckets (attached as a quick sheet):

- Blockers (must resolve before QBR): two items related to regional routing and log export format.
- High-priority (Q4 potential): retained audit-export cadence, and a feature toggle for per-tenant quantization profiles.
- Backlog (not Q4 feasible): interactive tooling for on-prem observability and multi-tenant key rotation UI.

ETA thoughts:
- Regional routing + log export format: we can commit to a narrow delivery window (targeting a small release) in 3 weeks if we prioritize and coordinate with infra.
- Per-tenant quantization toggle: requires design + ops gating; earliest feasible in 6-8 weeks without engineering tradeoffs.

I can present a single-slide tradeoff for the QBR that explains what’s doable before the end of Q4 and what needs a roadmap exception.

Marcus

Folks —

From a contractual standpoint:

- Data retention: committing to 7 years is feasible but requires an add-on fee and an opt-in to Private deployments (because hosted retention beyond 1 year expands storage and compliance obligations). We should be explicit to Acme about costs.
- SLA addendum: we can draft a scoped SLA for latency SLOs on Dedicated capacity only; we should avoid committing this for Hosted. LegalOps (cc) — can you prepare a first-pass addendum template?

For Acme's procurement timeline: they indicated they want a signed addendum before the internal QBR. If we cannot hit the 3-week delivery for regional routing, we should propose a partial commitment + staged deliverables.

Proposed immediate next step (owner assignments / due dates):
- Dev: perf runs with Acme payloads by 2026-10-19 EOD.
- Marcus: finalize the slide and ETA buckets by 2026-10-20 COB.
- Lauren: draft SLA addendum skeleton and costs by 2026-10-21.
- Evelyn: consolidate and respond to Acme with a clear canary/staged plan by 2026-10-21.

Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Product Operations | Redwood Inference

Thanks all — consolidating into a reply to Acme (draft below). Please flag any edits by EOD and I’ll send: 

--- DRAFT TO ACME ---
Hi Nora,

Appreciate the clarity on the exec asks. Summary of what we can commit to and next steps:

1) Latency SLOs: We can offer a p95 <120ms SLA on Dedicated capacity for models up to 13B with constraints (no >2 request batching; KV-prefix caching enabled). For larger models we will offer a staged fallback to a quantized 13B variant; full parity will require additional capacity costs.
2) Retention / audit exports: 7-year retention is available as a paid add-on and requires opting into Private or Dedicated with extended storage. We will include export tooling that supports quarterly exports; more frequent exports will incur additional ops fees.
3) Fallback behavior: we’ll deliver a deterministic fallback implementation to a smaller model family as a staged runtime change (ETA 2–5 weeks depending on canary results).

Planned near-term milestones: perf numbers (Dev) by 10/19 EOD; prioritization slide (Marcus) by 10/20 COB; SLA skeleton and pricing (Lauren) by 10/21. We propose a staged acceptance: initial addendum signing for SLA + 3-week routing deliverable, with a separate follow-up for the quantization toggle.

If that aligns, we’ll circulate an internal statement of work and a draft addendum for your legal team to review.

Best,
Evelyn
